report.verdict: A weak quarter that was then made almost irrelevant by Brazil: revenue -20% to EUR 10.4m (~$11.4m) and adj. EBITDA -30% to EUR 1.0m (~$1.1m) on a 52% collapse in SaaS EBITDA, while a Brazilian provisional measure banning fixed-odds betting removes the ~EUR 1.4m (~$1.5m) of Jan–Aug EBITDA — roughly 40-45% of the 9M group total on our arithmetic — and forced the July 2026-28 targets to be suspended. Record NDC volumes (+60%) and a 25.7% Affiliation margin show the operating engine still turns, but with cash at EUR 2.0m (~$2.2m), leverage back to 2.5x, a SEK 10m (~$1.0m) bond amortisation due in December and a failed bondholder consent in September, the equity is now a binary on the Brazilian Congress and on a 2027 refinancing.

summary: **Headline: a clear miss against the company's own July trajectory (there is no sell-side consensus for this First North micro-cap).** Revenue EUR 10,391k (~$11.4m), -20% YoY and -20.3% organic, -4% QoQ versus a restated Q2 of EUR 10,813k (~$11.9m); adj. EBITDA EUR 996k (~$1.1m), -30% YoY and -24% QoQ; adj. margin 9.6% (-130bps YoY, -250bps QoQ). Reuters/SquawkNews flashes corroborate revenue EUR 10.391m and EBITDA EUR 996k. Gaming Intelligence's headline of a '10% fall' conflicts with the company's -20%; we use the company figure.

**Brazil is the whole story.** On 25 Sep 2026 the Brazilian government signed a provisional measure prohibiting the operation, offering, intermediation and advertising of fixed-odds betting (sports and online casino) nationwide; operators had to disable Brazilian access by 6 Oct. Brazil has been one of Acroud's largest markets since the regulated framework started 1 Jan 2025 and generated ~EUR 1.4m (~$1.5m) EBITDA and ~EUR 0.8m (~$0.9m) net income in Jan–Aug 2026 — ~EUR 175k/month, which on our arithmetic is ~40-45% of group adj. EBITDA for the same period.

**Guidance: the 2026-28 targets were suspended, not revised — there is no new guidance.** The targets adopted 10 Jul 2026 (adj. EBITDA CAGR ~12%, i.e. FY28 adj. EBITDA of ~EUR 5.9m/~$6.4m off FY25's EUR 4.2m/~$4.6m; net debt/adj. EBITDA <1.25x by end-2028) were suspended on 28 Sep 'for as long as the regulatory uncertainty prevails'. Congress may approve, amend, reject or let the measure lapse within up to ~120 days (into late January 2027); management will reinstate targets only after that.

**SaaS drove the miss.** SaaS revenue EUR 6,919k (~$7.6m), -25% YoY against a record Q3-25 (EUR 9,258k/~$10.1m), with adj. EBITDA EUR 402k (~$0.44m), -52% YoY / -22% QoQ and margin 5.8% (-330bps). Management cites 'a slowdown in a smaller group of higher-margin markets within the Network Model' — markets not named. The slowdown pre-dates the Brazil measure, so it is not all Brazil, but a segment-level Brazil split was not provided.

**Affiliation EBITDA +4% YoY — but flattered by a cross-period reclass.** Affiliation revenue EUR 3,472k (~$3.8m), -8% YoY / -11.5% QoQ; adj. EBITDA EUR 894k (~$1.0m), +4% YoY at a 25.7% margin (+300bps). The segment footnote discloses EUR 136k (~$0.15m) of April–June revenue moved from SaaS into Q3 Affiliation 'including in the subtotals below EBITDA'. Stripping it (full drop-through assumed, our estimate), underlying Affiliation revenue is ~-12% YoY and EBITDA ~-12% YoY, not +4%.

**Volume up, monetisation sharply down.** Group NDCs hit a record 72,754 (+60% YoY): Affiliation 40,961 (+58%), SaaS Network 31,793 (+62%, all-time high). Against -20% revenue, revenue per NDC delivered fell ~42% in Affiliation (to ~EUR 85/~$93 from ~EUR 146/~$160) and ~54% in Network (to ~EUR 208/~$228 from ~EUR 454/~$498) — our calculation. Management itself warns NDC value 'varies greatly between regions' and that ~25% of Affiliation delivery historically came from Brazil.

**Sports-margin pass-through is now near-total.** Revenue-share rose to 89% of Affiliation revenue (79% in Q3-25), CPA fell to 8% (13%), other 3% (8%). Sports-betting affiliate revenue fell 19% to EUR 2,212k (~$2.4m) on 'lower realised operator margins' in the opening weeks of the European football season incl. the Champions League; casino rose 22% to EUR 1,260k (~$1.4m). Acroud is a price-taker on operator hold — no handle, structural margin or promo data exist for an affiliate.

**Cost base -19%, but mostly mechanical.** Opex ex items affecting comparability EUR 9,395k (~$10.3m), -19% YoY: SaaS opex -23% (network payouts flex with revenue), Affiliation opex -12%. Personnel EUR 1,214k (~$1.3m), -23% reported / -10% adjusted; other external expenses EUR 8,168k (~$9.0m), -20%. Management credits AI-enabled workflows for a 'substantial drop' in Affiliation personnel cost and promises SaaS efficiencies 'into 2027'. There is no quantified savings target, programme cost or target year — unlike a formal cost-transformation plan.

**Cash conversion collapsed.** CFO EUR 215k (~$0.24m) vs EUR 1,074k (~$1.2m), on lower EBITDA and an EUR 838k (~$0.9m) reduction in operating liabilities (net working-capital outflow EUR 676k/~$0.74m), despite tax paid of only EUR 106k (~$0.12m) vs EUR 575k. FCF (CFO+CFI) ~EUR 212k (~$0.23m); interest paid EUR 437k (~$0.48m) incl. EUR 99k (~$0.11m) final RIAE promissory-note interest. Cash fell to EUR 2,035k (~$2.2m) from EUR 2,298k (~$2.5m) at Q2.

**Leverage re-rose to 2.5x from 2.2x.** Interest-bearing net debt EUR 10,496k (~$11.5m), flat QoQ (EUR 10,452k) and -9% YoY, but LTM adj. EBITDA fell to ~EUR 4.26m (~$4.7m) by our sum of the last four quarters. Bonds: SEK 65.3m (~EUR 5.8m/~$6.3m) super senior at 10.5% due 31 Dec 2027 and SEK 70.8m (~EUR 6.3m/~$6.9m) restated senior at 10.75% due 30 Jun 2028; nominal SEK 136.1m ≈ EUR 12.0m (~$13.2m); gross debt SEK 145m (~EUR 12.8m/~$14.1m). A SEK 10m (~EUR 0.9m/~$1.0m) senior-bond amortisation falls due in December 2026 — c.43% of period-end cash.

**A liability-management attempt failed.** On 25 Aug Acroud launched a written procedure under the 2025/28 super senior bonds to amend the intercreditor agreement so it could make repurchase offers for the 2022/28 senior bonds (the two largest holders were supportive); on 9 Sep it withdrew the procedure citing 'diverging views among the broader bondholder base'. The discounted-buyback route to deleveraging is closed for now, and the bondholder base is visibly fragmented ahead of the Dec 2027 maturity.

**Restatement of Q1 and Q2 2026 (6 Nov).** Revenue and expenses of 'certain affiliate operations' were double-counted: revenue overstated by EUR 1.1m (~$1.2m) in each quarter (EUR 2.2m/~$2.4m for H1), all in Affiliation, with other external and personnel costs overstated by nearly the same amounts; EBITDA moved by only -EUR 22k/-20k, so H1 margin was restated up 120bps to 12.1%. Interim reports are not auditor-reviewed. Together with the Q3 EUR 136k reclass and a EUR 550k (~$0.6m) parent-level impairment of legacy SEO assets (eliminated on consolidation), financial-control quality is a live governance issue.

**Net loss narrowed only because of FX.** Net loss EUR -225k (~-$0.25m) vs EUR -681k (~-$0.75m), helped by a EUR 262k (~$0.29m) SEK/EUR translation gain on the bond within 'other financial items' (+EUR 243k vs -221k); interest expense EUR 491k (~$0.54m). Adjusted net loss (ex IAC and FX) doubled to EUR -450k (~-$0.49m) from -221k. Basic/diluted EPS rounds to EUR 0.00 (computed ~-EUR 0.0002/~-$0.0002) on 1,279m shares.

**The 9M picture still reads positively on paper — but the trend inverted in Q3.** 9M revenue EUR 31,686k (~$34.7m), -6%; adj. EBITDA EUR 3,527k (~$3.9m), +3%, margin 11.1% (+90bps); CFO EUR 2,103k (~$2.3m) vs 992k; net loss EUR -678k (~-$0.74m) vs -3,718k (which included a EUR 1,458k bond-extinguishment loss). Q4 will carry the Brazilian shutdown from 6 Oct.

**Intangibles exceed equity by ~1.5x — the Q4 impairment test matters.** Goodwill EUR 11,687k (~$12.8m) plus other intangibles EUR 13,801k (~$15.1m) = EUR 25.5m (~$27.9m) vs equity EUR 16,724k (~$18.3m; equity ratio 48%). Management states Brazil is 'not expected' to impair the Acroud Media CGU; its model assumes a 9-18% increase in EBITDA margin over five years, 2% terminal growth and an 11.9% post-tax WACC — generous against a 9.6% Q3 margin.

**Seasonality and events.** Q2/Q3 are structurally Acroud's weakest quarters (Q1/Q4 stronger). The 2026 World Cup knockout rounds (1–19 Jul) fell in Q3 but were not quantified; in Q2 management already conceded WC monetisation was below plan because its European-time-zone customer base was misaligned with the match schedule. Q3's call-out is instead the low operator hold in early-season European football.

**Ownership, liquidity and valuation context.** Only 722 shareholders; Saxo Bank nominee 36.4%, PMG Group (vendor of the acquired PMG companies) 15.2%, IBKR 9.6%, Sparekassen Danmark 9.1%, Trottholmen 5.4%. At the Q3-end price of SEK 0.12 (~$0.012) market cap is ~SEK 154m (~EUR 13.6m/~$14.9m); EV ~EUR 24m (~$26m), ~5.7x LTM adj. EBITDA on our numbers. ABG Sundal Collier is liquidity provider; FNCA is certified adviser.

**Management framing vs. what is buried.** The CEO letter leads with Brazil and 'record customer volumes', a 'cost base that continues to fall' and a 'materially repaired' balance sheet. Buried in footnotes: the EUR 136k cross-period segment reclass, the parent SEO impairment, the impairment-test assumptions, the working-capital drain behind the CFO collapse, and the fact that the SaaS 'high-margin markets' slowdown is unexplained geographically.

**Thesis read-through.** The equity is a levered option on (a) the Brazilian Congress rejecting or amending the measure by late January 2027 and (b) refinancing SEK 65.3m (~$6.3m) of 10.5% super senior paper due 31 Dec 2027. Absent Brazil, we estimate a run-rate adj. EBITDA of ~EUR 2.5-3.0m (~$2.7-3.3m) against ~EUR 12m (~$13.2m) of 10.5-10.75% bonds — leverage drifting to 3.5-4x. Bulls can point to record NDCs and a 24% 9M Affiliation margin; bears to a capital structure that cannot absorb losing its largest market. Next catalysts: Congress decision; Dec 2026 amortisation; Q4 impairment test; FY26 report on 25 Feb 2027.

segments.name: iGaming Affiliation (owned comparison/news sites; casino & sports betting)
segments.headline: Revenue -8% to EUR 3.5m (~$3.8m) on weak sports operator margins; EBITDA +4% at 25.7% margin, but flattered by a EUR 136k Q2 reclass and facing the loss of ~25% of NDC delivery from Brazil.
narrative: They report iGaming Affiliation revenue of EUR 3,472k (~$3.8m), down 8% year on year and 11.5% quarter on quarter against a restated Q2 of EUR 3,923k (~$4.3m), making the segment 33% of group revenue versus 29% a year ago. Casino rose 22% to EUR 1,260k (~$1.4m) while sports betting fell 19% to EUR 2,212k (~$2.4m), so the vertical mix moved to 36/64 casino/sports from 27/73. Management attributes the sports shortfall to lower realised operator margins during the opening weeks of the European football season, including the Champions League, and describes it as a recurring seasonal pattern in referred-player activity while conceding the data are too thin for statistical confidence. That reading is plausible, but it is also simply what a book that is now 89% revenue-share (79% in Q3-25), 8% CPA (13%) and 3% other (8%) looks like: Acroud has become a near-pure price-taker on operator hold, with the upside of recurring cohort annuities and the downside of quarterly hold volatility passing straight through. One footnote matters for the comparison: the segment number includes EUR 136k (~$0.15m) of April–June revenue that the Q2 report had presented in SaaS, so the clean Q3 figure is nearer EUR 3.34m (~$3.7m), roughly -12% year on year and -15% sequentially.

Customer delivery was the strongest on record at 40,961 NDCs, +58% year on year and +4% quarter on quarter (Q1 28,027; Q2 39,239), taking nine-month delivery to ~108k. Revenue per NDC delivered, on our arithmetic, fell to ~EUR 85 (~$93) from ~EUR 146 (~$160) in Q3-25 and ~EUR 100 (~$110) in Q2 — a 42% year-on-year decline that says the incremental player is lower value, from a lower-value geography, or shared with a partner; the company's own KPI definition notes that NDC value 'varies greatly between regions' and that the segment 'from time to time' splits NDC revenue with partners. More importantly, management disclosed that approximately 25% of the segment's player delivery has historically come from Brazil, which is subject to the prohibition from 6 October; mechanically that implies Q4 delivery could fall by a quarter before any redeployment of paid-media budgets. No market-share, #1/#2 ranking, monthly-active or ARPU data are disclosed — Acroud is a long-tail affiliate rather than a category leader, and NDCs are the only volume metric available.

By channel, SEO generated 55% of segment revenue (47% in Q3-25), paid media 37% (47%) and social/community-based affiliation 8% (6%). The Q2 report, published before the restatement, showed paid media at 70% and SEO at 23%, so either the double-counted 'certain affiliate operations' were paid-media driven or the mix is genuinely volatile quarter to quarter; either way the Q2 split is not comparable and we would not read the apparent swing to SEO as a strategic pivot until a restated Q2 channel mix is published. Paid-media exposure is relevant because it is cash-upfront, revenue-later under revenue-share — exactly the working-capital profile that depressed group operating cash flow this quarter — and because the parent company booked a EUR 550k (~$0.6m) impairment on legacy SEO assets during the quarter (eliminated on consolidation), an early admission that part of the historic SEO estate is no longer earning its carrying value.

Segment opex fell 12% year on year to ~EUR 2.58m (~$2.8m): other external expenses -14% to EUR 1,802k (~$2.0m) and personnel -8% to EUR 775k (~$0.85m), although personnel rose 5% sequentially against the restated Q2 figure of EUR 736k. Management credits AI-enabled workflows for a 'substantial drop' in Affiliation personnel cost, and the 9M segment opex decline of ~13% supports that something structural has happened. Adj. EBITDA was EUR 894k (~$1.0m), +4% year on year and -11% quarter on quarter, for a 25.7% margin (+300bps year on year, flat sequentially); nine-month EBITDA is EUR 2,784k (~$3.1m), +33%, at a 24.3% margin (+700bps). Adjusting for the EUR 136k reclass and assuming full drop-through, underlying Q3 EBITDA is ~EUR 0.76m (~$0.83m), about -12% year on year at a ~23% margin — still a respectable affiliate margin, but not the growth that management's framing implies. Segment D&A of EUR 853k (~$0.93m), overwhelmingly amortisation of acquired domains and intangibles, absorbs almost all of EBITDA, leaving segment EBIT of EUR 41k (~$0.04m) versus a EUR 35k loss a year ago.

Segment assets stand at EUR 21.9m (~$24.0m), down 15% year on year and dominated by goodwill and acquired intangibles that will be tested in Q4; management says the Brazilian developments are not expected to impair the Acroud Media CGU. No segment guidance is given; the stated priorities are cost discipline and converting the record NDC base into revenue-share annuities. Our read is that Q4 — seasonally the strongest quarter — will show whether the ~75% of delivery that sits outside Brazil can hold revenue around EUR 3.0-3.3m (~$3.3-3.6m) at a 22-25% margin (our estimate), which is what the group's leverage arithmetic now depends on. The quantified Brazil exposure (~EUR 1.4m/~$1.5m of group EBITDA in Jan–Aug) is not split by segment, but given the NDC disclosure we assume the larger part sits here.

segments.name: SaaS (Network Model – Matching Visions; Subscription Model – Voonix)
segments.headline: Revenue -25% to EUR 6.9m (~$7.6m) and adj. EBITDA -52% to EUR 0.4m (~$0.44m) at a 5.8% margin as 'higher-margin markets' slowed — the quarter's real negative, despite record network NDCs.
narrative: The SaaS segment — 67% of group revenue (71% a year ago) — comprises the Network Model, an affiliate-programme marketplace in which Acroud sits between operators and a long tail of SEO affiliates, streamers, media buyers and social influencers and retains a small slice of the revenue generated, and the Subscription Model, affiliate-tracking and business-intelligence software sold to affiliates and operators. They report revenue of EUR 6,919k (~$7.6m), -25% year on year and +0.4% quarter on quarter: Network EUR 6,605k (~$7.2m), -26% year on year, and Subscription EUR 314k (~$0.34m), -11% year on year but +2% sequentially. Management's explanation is 'a slowdown in a smaller group of higher-margin markets within the Network Model' against a Q3-25 comparison it calls 'exceptionally strong' (EUR 9,258k/~$10.1m, when group revenue grew 41%). The markets are not named. Because the slowdown pre-dates the 25 September Brazilian measure, it is not simply Brazil; but Brazil was one of the group's largest markets, the network model is precisely the vehicle through which a newly regulated market gets served quickly, and a segment-level Brazil split is the single disclosure we would press hardest for.

Volume again diverged from value. Network NDCs reached 31,793, +62% year on year and +12% quarter on quarter, another all-time high (Q1 22,276; Q2 28,319), taking nine-month network delivery to ~82k. Network revenue per NDC delivered, our calculation, fell to ~EUR 208 (~$228) from ~EUR 454 (~$498) a year ago and ~EUR 232 (~$255) in Q2 — a 54% year-on-year decline. Revenue Generating Units, the count of clients billed by the segment, slipped to 396, -5% year on year and -2% quarter on quarter (Q2-25 456; Q3-25 416; Q4-25 414; Q1-26 389; Q2-26 404), so revenue per RGU fell ~21% to ~EUR 17.5k (~$19.2k). Far more players, fewer billed clients and far less revenue per player is consistent with mix shifting toward lower-value geographies and lower-retention traffic types — the company's own description of the network is that it 'quickly pivots into pockets that are deemed attractive', which cuts both ways when a pocket closes.

Costs scale with the network: other external expenses, predominantly payouts to network affiliates, fell 24% to EUR 6,166k (~$6.8m), while personnel rose 15% to EUR 337k (~$0.37m); total segment opex was down 23% to ~EUR 6.5m (~$7.1m), slightly up sequentially. Because payouts flex with revenue, the headline 'SaaS opex -23%' is largely mechanical and says little about efficiency; management nonetheless flags 'further efficiencies expected within our SaaS Segment throughout the remainder of the year and into 2027' from the AI tooling piloted in Affiliation, with no amount attached. Adj. EBITDA was EUR 402k (~$0.44m), -52% year on year and -22% quarter on quarter (Q3-25 840; Q4-25 839; Q1-26 550; Q2-26 513), a 5.8% margin versus 9.1% a year ago and 7.4% in Q2 — 330bps of year-on-year compression that reflects the loss of higher-margin markets rather than cost creep. Nine-month adj. EBITDA is EUR 1,466k (~$1.6m), -24%, at 7.2% (-170bps). The EUR 136k Q2 reclass works the other way here: clean Q3 SaaS revenue is ~EUR 7.06m (~$7.7m), about -24% year on year, and clean EBITDA up to ~EUR 0.54m (~$0.59m), about -36% year on year, on our assumption of full drop-through.

Segment D&A is light at EUR 96k (~$0.1m), so segment EBIT of EUR 306k (~$0.34m), -55% year on year, remains the group's only meaningful operating-profit contributor; segment assets are EUR 11.6m (~$12.7m), -12% year on year. There is no segment guidance. Management calls SaaS its 'primary focus segment' and the scalable platform behind the suspended 12% EBITDA CAGR, which makes this quarter's margin print the most important negative in the release — more so than the Affiliation revenue decline. Market position is not quantified; the network's claimed moat is scale ('the more partnerships we build in the network, the more essential the product itself becomes'), but RGUs have fallen year on year in both of the last two reported quarters (-11% in Q2, -5% in Q3) and subscription revenue continues to decline year on year.

For Q4 we would watch whether the 'higher-margin markets' recover with seasonality, how the record Q3 NDC cohort converts into Q4 revenue, whether the subscription line stabilises around EUR 0.3m (~$0.33m), and for any quantified AI-driven opex reduction. We would model Q4 SaaS revenue of EUR 6.5-7.2m (~$7.1-7.9m) and adj. EBITDA of EUR 0.4-0.6m (~$0.4-0.7m) — our estimates — with downside if Brazilian network traffic proves to have been material to the mix.

Revenue Generating Units 396, -5% year on year, -2% quarter on quarter (Q2-25 456; Q3-25 416; Q4-25 414; Q1-26 389; Q2-26 404); revenue per RGU -21% to ~EUR 17.5k (~$19.2k).
Pattern is consistent with mix shifting toward lower-value geographies and lower-retention traffic types.

quote.text: quickly pivots into pockets that are deemed attractive
quote.speaker: Management

blocks.heading: Costs and EBITDA
blocks.takeaway: Adj. EBITDA fell 52% to EUR 402k (~$0.44m) at a 5.8% margin, 330bps compression driven by lost higher-margin markets, not cost creep.
points: Other external expenses, mainly affiliate payouts, -24% to EUR 6,166k (~$6.8m); personnel +15% to EUR 337k (~$0.37m); total opex -23% to ~EUR 6.5m (~$7.1m), slightly up sequentially.
Headline opex decline is largely mechanical as payouts flex with revenue; management flags further AI-driven efficiencies through 2027 with no amount attached.
EBITDA -22% quarter on quarter (Q3-25 840; Q4-25 839; Q1-26 550; Q2-26 513); margin 5.8% versus 9.1% a year ago and 7.4% in Q2.
Nine-month adj. EBITDA EUR 1,466k (~$1.6m), -24%, at 7.2% (-170bps).
Clean of the EUR 136k Q2 reclass, Q3 revenue is ~EUR 7.06m (~$7.7m), about -24%, and EBITDA up to ~EUR 0.54m (~$0.59m), about -36%.

blocks.heading: EBIT and positioning
blocks.takeaway: Segment EBIT of EUR 306k (~$0.34m), -55%, remains the group's only meaningful operating-profit contributor; this margin print is the release's most important negative.
points: D&A light at EUR 96k (~$0.1m); segment assets EUR 11.6m (~$12.7m), -12% year on year; no segment guidance.
Management calls SaaS its 'primary focus segment' and the scalable platform behind the suspended 12% EBITDA CAGR.
Market position not quantified; claimed moat is network scale, but RGUs fell year on year in both of the last two quarters (-11% in Q2, -5% in Q3) and subscription revenue keeps declining.

quote.text: the more partnerships we build in the network, the more essential the product itself becomes
quote.speaker: Management

blocks.heading: Q4 watch points
blocks.takeaway: We model Q4 SaaS revenue of EUR 6.5-7.2m (~$7.1-7.9m) and adj. EBITDA of EUR 0.4-0.6m (~$0.4-0.7m), with Brazil downside.
points: Watch whether 'higher-margin markets' recover with seasonality and how the record Q3 NDC cohort converts into Q4 revenue.
Watch whether subscription revenue stabilises around EUR 0.3m (~$0.33m) and for any quantified AI-driven opex reduction.
Downside if Brazilian network traffic proves material to the mix.

highlights.text: Record customer acquisition: 72,754 NDCs (+60% YoY, +8% QoQ) — Affiliation 40,961 (+58%) and SaaS Network 31,793 (+62%, all-time high); 9M NDCs 190,615 (+14%). Under an 89% revenue-share model this is future cohort revenue, if the players are in markets that stay open.

Affiliation margin expansion: adj. EBITDA EUR 894k (~$1.0m) at 25.7% (+300bps YoY); 9M segment EBITDA EUR 2,784k (~$3.1m), +33%, at 24.3% (+700bps) on opex -12% YoY, with AI-enabled workflows cutting personnel cost. Even stripping the EUR 136k (~$0.15m) reclass, underlying margin is ~23%.
Group opex ex IAC -19% YoY to EUR 9,395k (~$10.3m); personnel -10% adjusted to EUR 1,214k (~$1.3m); management guides to further SaaS efficiencies through Q4 and into 2027.

Balance-sheet repair since 2025 still shows: net debt EUR 10,496k (~$11.5m), -9% YoY; all non-bond debt (shareholder loan, RIAE promissory note) fully settled; 9M CFO EUR 2,103k (~$2.3m) more than doubled; equity ratio 48% (43%).
Casino affiliate revenue +22% YoY to EUR 1,260k (~$1.4m) (9M +34%), partly offsetting sports; revenue-share share rose to 89% from 79%, lowering CPA dependence.
Reported net loss narrowed 67% to EUR -225k (~-$0.25m), but EUR 262k (~$0.29m) of that is a SEK/EUR translation gain on the bond; adjusted net loss widened to EUR -450k (~-$0.49m).

lowlights.text: Brazil prohibition (signed 25 Sep, sites disabled 6 Oct): ~EUR 1.4m (~$1.5m) of Jan–Aug EBITDA and ~EUR 0.8m (~$0.9m) net income at risk — ~40-45% of group adj. EBITDA for the period on our arithmetic; 2026-28 financial targets suspended; ~25% of Affiliation NDC delivery historically Brazilian.

SaaS adj. EBITDA -52% YoY to EUR 402k (~$0.44m), margin 5.8% (-330bps), on an unexplained 'slowdown in a smaller group of higher-margin markets'; RGUs -5% to 396; subscription revenue -11% to EUR 314k (~$0.34m).
Monetisation deteriorating beneath the volume headline: revenue -20% organic while revenue per NDC fell ~42% in Affiliation (~EUR 85/~$93) and ~54% in Network (~EUR 208/~$228), our calculation.

Cash: CFO EUR 215k (~$0.24m) vs EUR 1,074k (~$1.2m) on a EUR 676k (~$0.74m) working-capital outflow; cash EUR 2,035k (~$2.2m) against a SEK 10m (~EUR 0.9m/~$1.0m) amortisation in December and ~EUR 0.35m (~$0.38m) of quarterly bond coupons.

Leverage back up to 2.5x (from 2.2x) on falling LTM EBITDA (~EUR 4.26m/~$4.7m); the August written procedure to permit senior-bond repurchases was withdrawn on 9 Sep after 'diverging views' among bondholders — the SEK 65.3m (~$6.3m) super senior tranche matures 31 Dec 2027.

Restatement of Q1/Q2 2026: revenue overstated EUR 1.1m (~$1.2m) per quarter (EUR 2.2m/~$2.4m H1) via double-counted affiliate operations; plus a EUR 136k (~$0.15m) cross-period/cross-segment reclass in Q3 and a EUR 550k (~$0.6m) parent impairment of legacy SEO assets; interims are not auditor-reviewed.

Sports-betting affiliate revenue -19% to EUR 2,212k (~$2.4m) on low operator hold in early-season European football; with 89% revenue-share exposure, Acroud now wears operator margin volatility in full, and management admits its seasonality data are 'too limited to draw firm statistical conclusions'.

forecast.intro: There is no conventional guidance to bridge. The only forward framework — the 2026-28 financial targets adopted on 10 Jul 2026 (adj. EBITDA CAGR of ~12%, implying FY28 adj. EBITDA of ~EUR 5.9m (~$6.4m) off FY25's EUR 4.2m (~$4.6m), and net debt/adj. EBITDA below 1.25x by end-2028) — was suspended on 28 Sep 2026 after Brazil's provisional measure, and the Q3 report repeats that updated targets will follow only once the Brazilian Congress has acted (validity up to ~120 days, i.e. into late January 2027). The driver is entirely the Brazilian exposure (~EUR 1.4m/~$1.5m of EBITDA in Jan–Aug 2026, ~EUR 175k/month), which touches both divisions: management says ~25% of Affiliation NDC delivery historically came from Brazil, and while it did not say so, we think the SaaS Network 'higher-margin markets' slowdown may be partly Brazil-linked. The quarter itself — adj. EBITDA EUR 996k (~$1.1m) versus the ~EUR 1.2m (~$1.3m) per quarter the 12% path implied (our estimate) — was already below the target trajectory before Brazil.

forecast.view: **Q4-26E (our estimates; the company gives none):** revenue EUR 9.0-10.0m (~$9.9-11.0m), -20% to -29% YoY against a Q4-25 base of EUR 12.6m (~$13.8m) that included a full Brazilian quarter; Q4 seasonality helps but cannot offset losing Brazil from 6 Oct. Adj. EBITDA EUR 0.4-0.7m (~$0.4-0.8m), margin 4-7%, versus EUR 733k (~$0.8m) in Q4-25, assuming the ~EUR 0.5m (~$0.55m) per-quarter Brazilian EBITDA run-rate drops out and SaaS opex cuts partly offset. **FY26E:** revenue ~EUR 40.7-41.7m (~$44.6-45.7m), -10% to -12% versus EUR 46.4m (~$50.8m) in FY25; adj. EBITDA EUR 3.9-4.2m (~$4.3-4.6m) versus EUR 4.2m (~$4.6m) — flat to down, not +12%. **Leverage:** the SEK 10m amortisation reduces gross debt and cash equally, so net debt only falls with free cash flow, which we put at EUR 0.2-0.5m (~$0.2-0.5m) in Q4; year-end net debt ~EUR 10.0-10.3m (~$11.0-11.3m), ND/adj. EBITDA **2.5-2.7x**, and year-end cash of only ~EUR 0.9-1.4m (~$1.0-1.5m) against ~EUR 1.4m (~$1.5m) of annual coupon at 10.5-10.75%. **FY27:** if the prohibition stands, a no-Brazil run-rate of EUR 2.5-3.0m (~$2.7-3.3m) adj. EBITDA implies leverage of 3.5-4.2x and makes the SEK 65.3m (~EUR 5.8m/~$6.3m) super senior maturity on 31 Dec 2027 a refinancing the business cannot self-fund — a further restructuring, exchange or equity raise becomes the base case. If Congress rejects or materially amends the measure by late January, FY27 adj. EBITDA could rebuild toward EUR 4.5-5.0m (~$4.9-5.5m) and ~2.0x leverage. **Swing factors:** (1) the Brazilian Congress outcome; (2) whether SaaS 'high-margin markets' recover in the seasonally stronger Q4 — the 52% EBITDA drop is the piece we understand least; (3) operator sports margins through the autumn football calendar (89% revenue-share exposure); (4) the Q4 impairment test on EUR 25.5m (~$27.9m) of goodwill and intangibles versus EUR 16.7m (~$18.3m) of equity, where a write-down would hit the 48% equity ratio and bond covenants; (5) bondholder appetite for any renewed amendment after the September withdrawal. **Margin direction:** down in Q4 (mix loss of high-margin Brazil) before cost actions can catch up; **revenue direction:** down double digits YoY through at least H1-27 on the Brazil lap; **leverage direction:** up.
watch: Brazilian National Congress decision on the provisional measure (validity up to ~120 days from 25 Sep 2026, i.e. into late January 2027): approve, amend, reject or lapse — and whether Acroud reinstates 2026-28 targets.
December 2026 SEK 10m (~EUR 0.9m / ~$1.0m) senior-bond amortisation versus EUR 2.0m (~$2.2m) cash; Q4 cash conversion and working-capital reversal.

Q4 annual goodwill/intangible impairment test (Acroud Media CGU): EUR 25.5m (~$27.9m) intangibles vs EUR 16.7m (~$18.3m) equity, model assuming 9-18% EBITDA-margin uplift over five years at 11.9% WACC.
Any renewed written procedure, bond repurchase or refinancing plan ahead of the 31 Dec 2027 super senior maturity (SEK 65.3m / ~$6.3m) and 30 Jun 2028 senior maturity (SEK 70.8m / ~$6.9m).
SaaS Network: recovery of the unnamed 'higher-margin markets', RGU trend (396, -5% YoY), revenue per NDC, and a quantified AI-driven opex reduction into 2027.
Affiliation: Q4 NDC delivery ex-Brazil (~25% historically Brazilian), revenue per NDC, sports operator hold through Q4, and the restated Q2 channel/vertical mix.
FY26 audit outcome on the restated H1 and the Q3 EUR 136k cross-period reclass; FY26 report due 25 Feb 2027.
